channel.title: Kseniia's Good News
channel.description: Positive news from several sources, scored 0-10 for goodness and refreshed every six hours.

item.title: Phase 1 trial of Ebola Bundibugyo vaccine begins in Uganda [6/10]
item.description: Scientists in Masaka have started an early trial of a candidate vaccine against the Bundibugyo Ebola strain, which has no licensed vaccine or treatment. (Goodness 6/10: Hopeful step, but early-stage and unproven.)

item.title: School meals reach over 250,000 children in Central African Republic [7/10]
item.description: The World Food Programme reports meals for more than 250,000 children in 335 schools across the Central African Republic, supporting local farmers. (Goodness 7/10: Helps many children, though aid-dependent.)

item.title: Free football academy in Rajasthan has trained over 5,000 children [7/10]
item.description: The Zinc Football Academy in Zawar covers fees, kit, hostel and food for players, and says more than 5,000 children have joined since 2017. (Goodness 7/10: Sustained opportunity for many young people.)

item.title: West Bengal programme teaches villagers to live safely near hyenas [6/10]
item.description: WINGS and partners run awareness sessions in Paschim Bardhaman so residents understand striped hyenas and respond safely after sightings. (Goodness 6/10: Local coexistence effort, modest scale.)

item.title: Report: most US homes could use heat pumps without straining grid [7/10]
item.description: An RMI report finds about 109 million US homes, roughly three-quarters, could adopt heat pumps without overloading the grid, possibly lowering rates and emissions. (Goodness 7/10: Removes a barrier to cleaner heating, but depends on uptake.)

item.title: Rural libraries in Minnesota and Washington open when unstaffed [6/10]
item.description: Some rural library systems let registered cardholders enter branches when no staff are present, and use is growing despite tight budgets. (Goodness 6/10: Widens access for people with limited free hours.)

item.title: Artificial mangrove roots slow coastal erosion in Thailand trial [6/10]
item.description: A 15-month trial in Samut Prakan province found artificial mangrove roots increased sediment build-up at 10 of 11 sites, with varying results. (Goodness 6/10: Promising stopgap, but results are uneven.)

item.title: Indonesian project tests mosque loudspeakers for earthquake alerts [7/10]
item.description: A five-year project is testing whether mosque loudspeakers can broadcast earthquake warnings from a sensor network. Uzbekistan plans a similar pilot. (Goodness 7/10: Practical idea that could save lives, still being tested.)

item.title: Georgia teen raises over $30,000 to give bikes to low-income families [6/10]
item.description: A teenager in Georgia founded a foundation that has given hundreds of bicycles to low-income families and taught hundreds of children to ride. (Goodness 6/10: Local youth initiative helping many families.)

item.title: Global mangrove cover rises after decades of loss [7/10]
item.description: Global Mangrove Watch data show mangrove cover grew by 477 square kilometres between 1985 and 2025, credited to restoration and stronger protection. (Goodness 7/10: Real reversal for a key ecosystem, though the gain is modest.)

item.title: Pittsburgh water authority launches debt forgiveness programme [6/10]
item.description: Pittsburgh's water authority will forgive overdue bills over 24 months for customers who keep up monthly payments. Some households were enrolled automatically from September. (Goodness 6/10: Eases household debt, but limited to one city's customers.)

item.title: Healthy-reef sounds help coral larvae settle on artificial reef [6/10]
item.description: Recordings of a healthy reef played through an underwater speaker in Hawai'i helped coral larvae settle on artificial structures. (Goodness 6/10: Early research with a creative approach to reef restoration.)

item.title: Warning patterns on wind turbine blades may protect birds [6/10]
item.description: In video-game-style experiments, great tits hesitated and approached less often when turbine blades carried warning patterns. (Goodness 6/10: Promising, but based on experiments rather than field deployment.)

item.title: Teenagers worldwide design projects to cut plastic use [7/10]
item.description: The Unplastify Challenge asks teenagers to design and carry out projects that reduce plastic use in their schools and communities. (Goodness 7/10: Youth-led action on plastic with real local projects, though scale is modest.)

item.title: Africa records the world's fastest gains in disaster resilience [7/10]
item.description: A new study finds Africa has made the world's fastest gains in disaster resilience. (Goodness 7/10: Real progress that protects many people from hazards.)

item.title: Two critically endangered Sumatran rhinos are pregnant [7/10]
item.description: Two Sumatran rhinos at an Indonesian sanctuary are pregnant, with calves due around May 2027, though experts warn about inbreeding. (Goodness 7/10: Hope for a species with very few individuals left, tempered by genetic risks.)

item.title: Largest known octopus nursery found off California [7/10]
item.description: Researchers found about 20,000 pearl octopuses gathered on the seafloor in Monterey Bay sanctuary, where warm springs shorten the brooding period. (Goodness 7/10: Notable discovery inside a protected area.)

item.title: Chennai conservationist helps over 80 schools welcome back house sparrows [7/10]
item.description: Koodugal Ganeshan advises schools to assess existing habitat before installing nest boxes so that campuses become better for house sparrows. (Goodness 7/10: Grassroots conservation spreading across schools.)

item.title: Argentine deep-sea canyon yields 57 species new to science [7/10]
item.description: Researchers identified 57 new species and five new genera from the Mar del Plata Canyon during a two-week workshop. (Goodness 7/10: A major biodiversity find, though it also highlights how little is protected.)

item.title: Scientists describe a giant fungus found in southwest China [6/10]
item.description: Researchers in southwest China described a new giant fungus, Dianjunus rex, whose upright fruiting bodies can reach about 20 inches tall, challenging ideas about fungal evolution. (Goodness 6/10: A new species adds to knowledge of life that is still being discovered.)

item.title: Indonesia releases 20 green sea turtles after Bali smuggling raid [6/10]
item.description: Authorities in Bali released 20 protected green sea turtles found alive on an abandoned boat during a smuggling attempt. (Goodness 6/10: Animals saved, though two did not survive and smuggling persists.)

item.title: Biomethane plant in southern Italy starts supplying renewable gas [6/10]
item.description: A plant in Grottole turns agricultural waste into a natural gas substitute and is expected to supply renewable gas to more than 3,000 homes. (Goodness 6/10: Cuts fossil gas use for a community by reusing farm waste.)

item.title: Maharashtra village uses job-scheme funds for watershed work that beat drought [7/10]
item.description: Hiware Bazar in Ahilyanagar district used Employment Guarantee Scheme funds for watershed works that restored farmland and brought migrant families home. (Goodness 7/10: Proven local model during a weak monsoon.)

item.title: Jharkhand's Mandar drum receives a Geographical Indication tag [6/10]
item.description: Artisans in Jarjatta village, Gumla, make the traditional Mandar drum from red clay and leather, and the craft now has GI recognition. (Goodness 6/10: Cultural recognition for local artisans.)

item.title: Artist paints Britain's restored nature in new exhibition [6/10]
item.description: Rebecca Howard's paintings celebrate nine projects that are restoring nature across Britain. (Goodness 6/10: Uplifting culture piece tied to ongoing rewilding work.)

item.title: Congolese NGO to co-manage Itombwe Nature Reserve in a DRC first [7/10]
item.description: Strong Roots Congo will co-manage Itombwe Nature Reserve in South Kivu with the national wildlife authority, the first such arrangement in the country. (Goodness 7/10: Local stewardship of a protected area is a meaningful step for conservation.)

item.title: Student-run housing offers safe spaces for unhoused young adults [7/10]
item.description: Projects such as Aggie House at UC Davis and Y2Y in Cambridge, Massachusetts provide low-cost or short-term housing for young people without homes. (Goodness 7/10: Practical community solutions that help a vulnerable group.)

item.title: Indian Supreme Court treats menstrual health as part of right to life [7/10]
item.description: A ruling treats menstrual health as part of the right to life. A ten-point checklist helps parents assess their daughter's school facilities. (Goodness 7/10: Legal recognition that could improve school facilities for many girls.)

item.title: Floating shades help coral survive a marine heatwave [6/10]
item.description: Divers placed floating shades over 20 brain coral colonies in the Florida Keys, which regained colour while unshaded colonies stayed bleached. (Goodness 6/10: A cheap local tool for reefs, but limited in scale.)

item.title: Teen leads student effort to curb crop burning in West Bengal [7/10]
item.description: Sixteen-year-old Sk Reezaal Arafat leads SATARK, a student climate-tech initiative using satellite data, low-cost sensors and fieldwork to anticipate and reduce crop residue burning. (Goodness 7/10: Local youth action against air pollution, small in scale so far.)

item.title: Plan to link and green London's outer edges announced [7/10]
item.description: Organisers of a London project say it will reconnect wilder green spaces around the capital, aiming to benefit about ten million people and boost biodiversity. (Goodness 7/10: Large urban nature plan, but still a plan not yet delivered.)

item.title: Berlin app lets residents adopt and water thirsty street trees [6/10]
item.description: The open-source app Gieß den Kiez maps roughly 900,000 street trees and lets Berliners water them, helping the city's trees through heatwaves. (Goodness 6/10: Practical citizen-led way to protect urban trees.)

item.title: Teen's lemonade stand grows into a $5 million charity effort [6/10]
item.description: An Ohio teen who wanted to return kindness she once received built a lemonade stand into a fundraiser supporting children's hospitals and toy donations. (Goodness 6/10: Good for local children's causes, limited in scale.)

item.title: Chinook salmon reclaim most of their historic Klamath River habitat after dam removal [8/10]
item.description: Within two years of four dams being removed from the Klamath River, Chinook salmon recolonized about 88% of their known historical habitat. (Goodness 8/10: Rapid ecological recovery after dam removal.)

item.title: First Nation-led project replants kelp forests in Clayoquot Sound [7/10]
item.description: The Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation and partners launched a kelp nursery in early 2026 and are restoring kelp forest in Clayoquot Sound. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led marine restoration, still early.)

item.title: Forest ecologist who listens to rainforests wins environmental award [6/10]
item.description: Zuzana Burivalova of the University of Wisconsin-Madison won the 2026 Pritzker Emerging Environmental Genius Award for her remote-sensing and sound-based forest research. (Goodness 6/10: Recognition for conservation science.)

item.title: Kenya reports no new Ebola cases since first death [6/10]
item.description: Kenyan authorities say no new cases have been found since a patient died on October 5, with none of 293 samples testing positive. (Goodness 6/10: Containment looks good so far, but vigilance continues.)

item.title: Passive cooling explored as low-energy option in Colombo [6/10]
item.description: Residents of dense Colombo apartment blocks rely on fans and air conditioning. Sri Lanka is exploring passive cooling methods as an energy-saving alternative, though with costs. (Goodness 6/10: A practical energy-saving idea, still at an exploratory stage.)

item.title: Community leader describes marine conservation in Cambodia [7/10]
item.description: A commune deputy chief on Koh Sdach discusses community-led marine conservation, balancing fishing livelihoods with ecological protection through a community fisheries management area. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led conservation that supports local livelihoods.)

item.title: Family sells 650 acres on East Texas lake for a state park [6/10]
item.description: A multigenerational family sold 650 acres on Lake Palestine to become a state park. The land includes pine woods, bluffs, wetlands and a pecan orchard. (Goodness 6/10: Protected land opens to the public, a local benefit.)

item.title: Ten minutes of daily exercise linked to deeper sleep [6/10]
item.description: A University of Texas at Austin study linked more frequent exercise to more deep sleep. About 10 minutes of moderate to vigorous activity a day showed measurable benefits. (Goodness 6/10: Simple, accessible health finding, but it shows association only.)

item.title: Australia sets a renewable energy record led by rooftop solar [8/10]
item.description: On 22 September solar and wind supplied 80.4 percent of demand on Australia's national grid, with rooftop panels briefly carrying over half the load. The annual renewable share is 44 percent. (Goodness 8/10: Record clean power share, though the annual figure is lower.)

item.title: Changing gait may ease knee arthritis pain [6/10]
item.description: Scientists report that adjusting how a person walks can relieve knee arthritis pain about as well as prescription drugs, and may slow cartilage wear. (Goodness 6/10: A drug-free option for a common condition, though details of evidence are limited.)

item.title: Aldabra giant tortoise count reaches about 180,000 [8/10]
item.description: A survey on Aldabra Atoll in the Seychelles counted about 180,000 giant tortoises, the highest figure recorded. The species was once considered endangered. (Goodness 8/10: A recovered, once-endangered species at a record population.)

item.title: Woman electrician keeps power running for a Maharashtra village [6/10]
item.description: Jyoti Sarjerao has worked with the state electricity department and is the person her village calls when the power fails. (Goodness 6/10: Inspiring local profile that breaks a gender barrier.)

item.title: Festival food offerings in Mumbai turned into electricity [7/10]
item.description: About 39 tonnes of leftover food from the Lalbaugcha Raja festival were processed into electricity for a hospital project. (Goodness 7/10: Practical reuse of food waste for a public service.)

item.title: Kenyan children learn chess on sets made from recycled plastic [7/10]
item.description: A community project recycled about 200 kg of plastic into chess sets, teaching children the game while reducing waste. (Goodness 7/10: Small community project combining recycling and education.)

item.title: Carthage Music Days festival features artists from 15 countries [6/10]
item.description: The 11th Carthage Music Days festival ran for a week in Tunis with artists from 15 countries, putting emphasis on the local scene. (Goodness 6/10: A cultural event supporting local musicians.)

item.title: Seed-sized injectable device could treat chronic pain by controlling nerves [6/10]
item.description: A tiny injectable device regulates nerve activity without batteries or wires and could offer a new approach to chronic pain. (Goodness 6/10: Potential relief for many people, but still early research.)

item.title: Sloth bear rescued from India's dancing trade is now thriving [6/10]
item.description: A sloth bear rescued in 2009 from being forced to dance for tourists is reported by a rescue charity to be doing well in its sanctuary home. (Goodness 6/10: Animal rescued from cruelty and now healthy, though it is a single animal.)

item.title: Solar-powered truck processes waste before it reaches landfill [6/10]
item.description: A 22-foot solar-powered mobile unit sorts, shreds and processes waste on site, reducing what goes to landfills. (Goodness 6/10: Practical local waste solution, small scale.)

item.title: Lost model by Trevi Fountain sculptor found in salvage yard [6/10]
item.description: A 27-inch model by sculptor Pietro Bracci was found in a British reclamation yard for about 300 pounds. It was a pitch for a bronze statue of Pope Clement XII. (Goodness 6/10: A pleasant cultural rediscovery with limited wider impact.)

item.title: Ethiopia pursues massive tree-planting campaign to restore forests [6/10]
item.description: Ethiopia is working to replant forests lost to clearing through a large-scale seedling campaign, though challenges remain. (Goodness 6/10: Ambitious restoration with results still to be proven.)

item.title: Women rangers prepare to release Darwin's rheas in Chilean Patagonia [7/10]
item.description: A women-led ranger team is preparing to release 13 Darwin's rheas at Patagonia National Park in Chile to help restore the species. (Goodness 7/10: Local restoration effort for a native bird.)

item.title: Women-led rangers prepare to return Darwin's rheas to Chilean Patagonia [7/10]
item.description: A women-led ranger team is getting ready to release 13 Darwin's rheas into Patagonian habitat as part of a reintroduction effort. (Goodness 7/10: Concrete wildlife restoration led by a local team.)

item.title: Volunteers remove 18,000 kg of plastic from a Mumbai beach in a day [7/10]
item.description: More than 1,500 volunteers cleared 18,000 kilograms of marine plastic from a Mumbai shoreline in one day. (Goodness 7/10: Large community clean-up with visible results.)

item.title: Painting one wind turbine blade black sharply cut bird deaths [7/10]
item.description: A long-term study at a Spanish wind farm found that painting a single turbine blade black greatly reduced annual bird fatalities. (Goodness 7/10: Cheap, practical fix for wind power's wildlife impact.)

item.title: Navi Pillay wins the Nobel Peace Prize [7/10]
item.description: South African-born jurist Navi Pillay has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, recognising her work in international justice. (Goodness 7/10: Major recognition for human rights work.)

item.title: Indigenous youth in Ecuador use rap to defend the Amazon [6/10]
item.description: Young Amazonian artists rap in Kichwa and other languages to draw attention to threats to their forests and communities. (Goodness 6/10: Community-driven advocacy and cultural vitality.)

item.title: Victoria, Australia creates three new national parks [8/10]
item.description: About 650 square kilometres of forest in Victoria becomes three national parks, including the large Wombat-Lerderderg park, protecting gliders, owls and other wildlife. (Goodness 8/10: Large new protected habitat for wildlife.)
